title: Alleged electricity theft and the assessed amount

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. Power cut over alleged theft: does the consumer get a hearing on the bill, and can a court restore supply on half the bill?
Twenty sixth October, twenty twenty six: the Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Manoj Misra and Honourable Justice K V Viswanathan ruled.
scenes.shown: 26 October 2026: the Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Manoj Misra and Honourable Justice K.V. Viswanathan ruled.

scenes.dialogue: In January twenty twenty four, Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company issued a supplementary bill to a consumer accused of electricity theft.
scenes.shown: In January 2024, Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company issued a supplementary bill to a consumer accused of electricity theft.

scenes.dialogue: The bill was nearly ninety three lakh rupees, plus compounding charges. A Single Judge of the Gujarat High Court ordered reconnection once half was deposited.
scenes.shown: The bill was nearly ₹93 lakh, plus compounding charges. A Single Judge of the Gujarat High Court ordered reconnection once half was deposited.

scenes.dialogue: The Division Bench let the consumer object to the bill before the Executive Engineer, and, if it lost, appeal under Section One Twenty Seven of the Act.
scenes.shown: The Division Bench let the consumer object to the bill before the Executive Engineer, and, if it lost, appeal under Section 127 of the Act.

scenes.dialogue: The distribution company argued: in theft cases there is no right to object or appeal, since the Special Court fixes civil liability. And half is too lenient.
The Supreme Court held: the Act has no assessment provision except Section One Twenty Six. So the amount to deposit for reconnection follows that same procedure.
scenes.shown: The Supreme Court held: the Act has no assessment provision except Section 126. So the amount to deposit for reconnection follows that same procedure.

scenes.dialogue: That means a provisional assessment, a hearing on objections, and an appeal. Where a complaint is filed, the Special Court decides civil liability.
Theft cases demand caution. But if the provisional assessment is prima facie arbitrary, the High Court may restore supply on at least half. Both appeals failed.
